discovery.about: obscura, the embeddable Rust library API over the engine: Browser, Page, Element and CookieStore, with request interception and many engine regression tests.
discovery.see: Crate readme for the embeddable API: driving a real V8 and DOM browser (Browser, Page, Element, CookieStore) from Rust without CDP, depending on it via git because it compiles V8, and a usage example with stealth and a storage directory.
The library Page and Element types: goto, content, url, evaluate, query_selector and wait_for_selector, settle, interception hooks and element text and attribute access with escaped attribute names.

Browser and BrowserBuilder: Browser::new, builder options for proxy, stealth, user agent and storage directory, new_page creating pages that share one browser context, and cookies() returning the session's CookieStore.
BrowserConfig and BrowserConfigBuilder holding launch options for a Browser instance: proxy URL, stealth flag, user agent override and storage directory, with a builder pattern ending in build().
The Cookie type exposed to Rust callers and CookieStore with set from a Set-Cookie string and URL, get_all, get_for_url, and save_to_file and load_from_file for persisting a session's cookies.
Example program: builds a stealth Browser with a storage directory, opens a page, navigates to example.com, prints URL and content length, and waits for a link to read its text and href.

End-to-end test of the request and response interception API (issue 306) against a minimal local HTTP server: preload scripts, the interception channel and passive on_request and on_response for JS fetch and XHR.
Issue 600 regression: a child iframe's document was fetched and parsed but never got a scripting context; scripts inside the frame must run, tested with two documents served from one local server.
Issue 756 regression: dropping one Page while another is still alive must not abort the process, because each Page owns its own V8 isolate on the same thread and isolate enter and exit order matters.
Security regression SEC-007 (issue 583): Element::attribute must escape the attribute name so a quote cannot break out of the generated getAttribute script and run arbitrary page JavaScript.
Issue 663 regression: fetch and XHR must always run URL resolution for relative URLs, even when the query string contains an absolute URL such as api/proxy?target=https://cdn/x.json.
Issue 394 regression: new Image() must survive pages that predefine a non-configurable src property on img elements, as some anti-bot instrumentation does.

Select element parity needed by jQuery and WooCommerce variation forms: a single select without a selected attribute implicitly selects its first option, so selectedIndex is 0 and value reflects that option.
Textarea parity (issue 685): the element now has its own interface and control geometry, so an empty textarea is no longer a zero-height full-width block that Playwright resolves as hidden.
Tests that XMLHttpRequest with responseType arraybuffer returns the response bytes unchanged; XHR is implemented over fetch and previously decoded every body as text, corrupting binary data.
Tests that the stealth transport is used only when compiled in and enabled at runtime, by comparing the user agent a local server sees for navigations with and without stealth.
